keyVerseText: And Joelah, and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.
rootMeaning: The root of יוֹעֵאלָה (Yôwʻêʼlâh) comes from the Hebrew verb יַעַל (yaʻal), which fundamentally means 'to ascend' or 'to gain.' In its idiomatic and Hiphil form, it conveys the idea of profiting, benefiting, or availing oneself. The name יוֹעֵאלָה thus carries the sense of 'may he avail' or 'may he be of benefit,' implying a person who is effective, valuable, or able to accomplish good. This root meaning enriches the name beyond a mere label, suggesting a character marked by usefulness and strength.
usageInScripture: The word יוֹעֵאלָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 12:7, where it is translated as 'Joelah.' This consistent singular use as a proper name for an individual, one of David's mighty warriors, indicates the name's function as an identifier rather than a common noun. The translation 'And Joelah' reflects its role in the text as a marker of a person who is part of a significant group, highlighting the name's association with strength and valor.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יוֹעֵאלָה as 'may he avail' reminds believers that God equips His people to be effective and beneficial in their service. This name, borne by one of David's mighty men, reflects the biblical theme that God calls and empowers individuals to accomplish His purposes. The root meaning of availing or profiting aligns with the Christian faith's emphasis on fruitful service and spiritual efficacy through God's enabling. It encourages believers to trust that their efforts, when aligned with God's will, will indeed 'avail' and contribute to His kingdom.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 12:7, the mention of 'Joelah, the son of Jeroham of Gedor,' situates him among David's loyal warriors. The name's meaning, 'may he avail,' enriches this verse by suggesting that Joelah was not just a name on a list but a man empowered to be effective in battle and leadership. It underscores the trustworthiness and strength of those who supported David, highlighting how God’s provision enables His people to stand firm and accomplish His purposes.
